dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "dealer_import_log.csv (rows 37, 38) & recharges.csv"
"Batch DF-00020 (DLR-104) contains 8 valid rows matching 8 annual renewals totaling $723.42."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The cluster of 17 West-region annual-plan renewals posted on 31 May represents genuine, non-duplicate revenue that was contractually batched and processed during the month-end commission close."
"The import log shows that both batches (DF-00020 and DF-00040) had 0 duplicates, 0.0 USD reconciliation difference, and were successfully reconciled on May 31."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Rejected Hypotheses"
"While the email confirms monthly batching is contractually permitted, a copy of the active dealer contracts for DLR-104 and DLR-219 would be required to verify the exact terms."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Accept the May revenue as reported and close the review."
"Update the anomaly detection thresholds in the weekly trend pack to exclude contractually batched month-end uploads to prevent future false positives."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "No Material Issue."
"A query of the entire recharges database shows these 17 subscribers have no other historical recharges, confirming no double billing occurred."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "genuine, non-duplicate revenue" is stronger than the evidence shown: uniqueness and reconciliation support no duplicate cash or duplicate source records, but the submission does not demonstrate the underlying entitlement or event timing.

"Dealer contracts permit monthly submission of annual renewals" is attributed to an email, which is corroboration rather than proof of the active contract terms; the submission itself acknowledges that the contracts were not inspected.
"A query of the entire recharges database" is asserted without the query, fields, or reproducible result, and "confirming no double billing occurred" overstates what the stated checks establish.

"Exclude contractually batched month-end uploads" could suppress future genuine anomalies unless the rule is tied to verified dealer configuration and accompanied by reconciliation monitoring. The submission does not show that the 17 business events occurred throughout the month or address effective_event_date.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The spike is a benign posting-time quirk for two dealers: annual-plan business events occurred across the month, while dealer commission-reconciliation files were uploaded on 31 May with original effective dates. The analyst handled the no-duplicate-revenue explanation but missed the important alternative implication that posting-time batching can still distort event-time retention and trend analytics.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Compare posted_at with effective_event_date for all 17 renewals and explicitly report the event-date distribution, then join the import log to verify unique source_event_ids, entitlement/cash reconciliation, and downstream analytics impact before closing the review.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The repeat caller rate increased from 16.3% under LEGACY to 57.1% under the NOVA-S1 pilot."
"40.4% of unique callers (573 out of 1,420) were stranded in the IVR, ending in an ERROR or ABANDONED state without reaching an agent."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The drop in complaint cases in the South region is not due to improved customer experience, but is a result of technical errors in the NovaIVR pilot (NOVA-S1) that blocked and stranded 40.4% of unique callers during authentication"
"The containment dashboard ignores all failed sessions that end prior to successful subscriber identification."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Unknowns: We lack CSAT/NPS survey results to confirm if customers who hung up during self-service were satisfied or simply frustrated by the system's inability to transfer them."
"Self-Service Improved CX: Rejected. If self-service resolved customer issues, repeat calls would decrease."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Do NOT expand the pilot nationally."
"Revert the South-region IVR routing to the LEGACY version immediately to restore customer access to care agents."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "What specific technical work is being done to address the high volume of TOKEN_MISMATCH (200) and ANI_LOOKUP_TIMEOUT (146) errors in the authentication module?"
"Do not proceed with national expansion until the technical bugs causing TOKEN_MISMATCH and ANI_LOOKUP_TIMEOUT are resolved."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The submission states that the reduction is definitively "not due to improved customer experience" even though it acknowledges that satisfaction among abandoned callers is unknown.

It describes all 573 ERROR or ABANDONED callers as "blocked and stranded" and attributes them to technical errors, although abandonment is not itself evidence of a complaint or technical failure, and the submission does not distinguish error, voluntary abandonment, and unresolved need.

"Many users who got a \"RESOLVED\" status ... called back hours later" is supported only by the cited example of subscriber SWD-0000041 as presented; no cohort-level rate or timing analysis is provided.
The recommendation to "Revert ... immediately" is stronger than the evidence-based recommendation to pause national inference and preserve the pilot while validating end-to-end outcomes.
The questions assert that sessions without case creation or transfer were incorrectly logged as "RESOLVED," but the submission does not provide the relevant counts, rules, or row-level evidence.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst partially handled the alternative that some abandoned callers may have been satisfied by explicitly stating that CSAT/NPS is unknown. However, it missed the strongest benign interpretation: some abandonment may represent successful self-service or a caller choosing not to continue, while repeat calls may reflect a new or unrelated need rather than failure of the prior interaction. It also did not triangulate South service-event exposure or sampled calls to distinguish these possibilities.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Replace the definitive causal conclusion and immediate rollback with an end-to-end validation plan: link IVR sessions to case creation, transfers, repeat contacts, and subsequent outcomes; separate authentication errors from ordinary abandonment; and review a stratified sample of calls before deciding whether to roll back or expand.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites inverter_events.csv for the claims that all four events have impact_mw = 0, cleared = yes, and occurred from 08:06 to 16:18.
The claim that the export is "heavily filtered or incomplete" is not tied to a field or independent comparison; it is inferred only from "4 rows over a 9-day period."

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission asserts that "a communication loss (COMM_LINK_WARN) prevents the SCADA system from collecting actual generation data" without checking independent power telemetry, raw SCADA values, inverter status, or an unfiltered event source.
The stated rejected hypothesis is internally confused: it says the warning represents zero actual impact, then gives a mechanism in which the recorded zero is merely a default caused by missing data.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission labels the communication-loss/default-zero mechanism as the reason for rejecting the hypothesis, but provides no uncertainty or evidence that this mechanism actually occurred.
The possibility that four events reflect normal sparse transient warnings, rather than an incomplete export, is not considered.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: "Perform one cheap check by verifying the SCADA database export filters" is low-risk and directionally relevant to the export-completeness concern.

The proposed check is not sufficiently discriminating because it does not specify comparison with raw records or independent MW telemetry around an event, and it does not explicitly recognize the zero-impact and cleared-event evidence.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion appropriately recommends a limited check rather than escalating a plant problem.

However, it is based on the overstated finding that the small log "suggests a heavily filtered or incomplete export" and does not make the better-supported qualification that the events show no demonstrated MW impact and may simply be transient communications or check warnings.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The four-row, nine-day log is described as suggesting a "heavily filtered or incomplete export" without a baseline, expected event rate, or comparison to raw data.
The claim that COMM_LINK_WARN causes SCADA to default impact_mw to zero is unsupported by the cited evidence.
The communication hypothesis is described as rejected even though the explanation offered is consistent with a data-quality artifact rather than evidence against it.
The submission does not establish that the daytime timing is anomalous or causally relevant.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The warnings may be ordinary transient communications or input-check events: all recorded events have 0 MW impact and cleared=yes, so the visible evidence does not demonstrate a plant-generation problem. The small event count alone may be normal rather than evidence of filtering.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Compare one or more affected timestamps against raw SCADA/inverter telemetry and the unfiltered event table, checking both actual MW and event-record presence; this would distinguish a real zero-impact transient from a default zero caused by missing communications and test the export-filter hypothesis directly.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites dispatch_blocks.csv and DSM_Commercial_Extract.pdf for the same-day counterfactual and gives specific values: 549,664 Rs counterfactual penalty, 96,578 Rs savings, and 17.57%.
It identifies the 29 May pilot blocks as blocks 53 to 64 and reports the exact 0.96135 multiplier, making the central calculation reproducible from the cited data.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission correctly distinguishes the cross-day comparison from the same-day comparison: “The 31.6% DSM penalty reduction claim is not supported” because 28 May and 29 May differ in weather and stowing conditions.
It tests an innocent explanation—daily variability associated with later stowing and different total generation—and constructs the relevant same-day base-schedule counterfactual.

The statement that “Only 96,578 Rs (46%) was directly caused by the pilot's schedule scaling” treats a model-based counterfactual difference as established causation, rather than clearly labeling it as the pilot's modeled or estimated contribution.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission appropriately states that a single pilot day cannot establish whether the flat scaling is optimal or generalizes across wind speeds.
It retains a positive same-day result rather than overcorrecting to no value, reporting a 17.57% modeled DSM reduction and 13.1% generation-gap reduction.

The high-confidence wording and “directly caused” language are too strong for a one-day, non-randomized counterfactual analysis; uncertainty in the counterfactual model and attribution is not quantified.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation to retain the workbook for further evaluation but not expand nationally follows the single-day evidence and the stated limitation that performance across wind conditions is unknown.

The proposed multi-week validation is directionally useful and seeks control comparisons, but randomized inverter subsets may face interference or shared-weather confounding, and alternating high-wind days is not by itself a strong randomized design.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion accurately rejects the uncontrolled 31.6% headline while preserving the smaller same-day modeled benefit: “the pilot revisions contributed to a 17.6% marginal reduction in DSM penalty and a 13.1% marginal reduction in the generation gap.”

This matches the supplied causal limitation: the different-day comparison is not controlled, but the base_schedule_mw versus submitted_schedule_mw comparison on 29 May supports a directionally favorable pilot-day counterfactual result.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “Only 96,578 Rs (46%) was directly caused by the pilot's schedule scaling” is overstated. The evidence supports a same-day counterfactual or model-implied incremental difference, not definitive causal attribution.

The allocation of 112,780 Rs to “natural daily variability” is plausible and may be arithmetically derived from the two comparisons, but the submission does not explain a validated decomposition that isolates all non-pilot causes.
The proposed A/B design is not fully specified to address dependence among inverters, shared weather, changing stowing times, and operational spillovers.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The pilot day performed better and the submitted schedule is associated with a meaningful same-day modeled improvement, but the observed 17.6% penalty reduction could still differ from the true causal effect because the counterfactual depends on schedule and penalty-model assumptions.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Reframe the 96,578 Rs and 42.5 MWh figures explicitly as model-based same-day counterfactual estimates, then specify a matched or randomized validation with pre-defined weather, stowing-time, and operational covariates and uncertainty intervals.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The broker declared tariff code 90211000 for Product P1001 (Titanium acetabular cup)." — Source: "declaration.pdf"
"The approved Swiss tariff code for Product P1001 is 90211000." — Source: "country_tariff_matrix.xlsx (Swiss Matrix sheet)"
"Helios records the global/EU code 90211090 for Product P1001." — Source: "product_master_current.xlsx"
The submission explicitly identifies a limitation: "A direct lookup in the official Swiss Customs Tariff database (Tares) ..." is missing.

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: The submission tests and rejects the broker-error hypothesis: "The broker entered 90211000, which matches the approved Swiss Matrix code for P1001 exactly."
It offers a mechanism for the discrepancy: "the automated tool flagged it because it compared it to the Helios code 90211090 without accounting for Swiss local nomenclature."
The reasoning does not test whether the internal Swiss Matrix itself is current or legally authoritative, despite acknowledging missing Tares verification.

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: The evidence table assigns "High" confidence to the declaration, Swiss Matrix, Helios record, and Read Me claims.
The submission appropriately identifies unresolved uncertainty: "A direct lookup in the official Swiss Customs Tariff database (Tares) ..." is missing.
However, the categorical decision "Do NOT escalate" and conclusion "is a false positive" are stronger than the stated evidence because legal coverage of code 90211000 has not been verified.

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: The submission explains the data-lineage mismatch between "a Swiss local tariff code" and "a global/EU database."
It distinguishes the broker declaration, Swiss Matrix, and Helios product-master records rather than treating the differing strings as independent proof of misconduct.

The explanation would be stronger with evidence of the comparison engine's actual jurisdiction-selection or mapping logic; it currently relies on the Read Me description and the observed code difference.

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: The proposed action is operationally proportionate in recognizing the mismatch: "Update the automated comparison engine to map Swiss declarations using the Swiss Matrix sheet rather than the global Helios database."

But it recommends immediate irreversible-seeming disposition: "Mark the flag ... as a 'false positive' and clear it in the system" while explicitly noting that "A direct lookup in the official Swiss Customs Tariff database (Tares)" remains outstanding.
A safer action would be to classify or suppress the alert provisionally, preserve the audit trail, and complete Tares validation before final clearance or broad engine changes.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Do NOT escalate" and "is a false positive" are not fully established because the submission has not verified in Tares that 90211000 legally covers the stated implant.

"Swiss local nomenclature uses different tariff codes than the EU CN8 matrix, making direct string matching across jurisdictions invalid" is plausible and attributed to the workbook Read Me, but the submission does not quote or independently validate that passage.

"Update the automated comparison engine" is a reasonable remediation direction, but the submission does not establish that the Swiss Matrix is the authoritative, current mapping source for all relevant Swiss declarations.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The discrepancy is most likely a benign Swiss-versus-global/EU code-system mismatch, but an incorrect broker declaration or an outdated/internal Swiss Matrix cannot be conclusively excluded until the official Tares lookup and the comparison engine's jurisdiction and mapping logic are verified.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Complete and cite the Tares lookup for 90211000 and verify the comparison engine's jurisdiction-selection and mapping rules before permanently clearing the alert or deploying the proposed mapping change.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The supplier declaration reference for SUP-02 / P1006 was expired as of 31 July 2025 (shipment date was 18 September 2025)."
"The EU has no free trade agreement (FTA) with the US that allows preferential duty-free imports. | Customs Rules"
"Confidence" values are uniformly marked "High," without stating any source limitations.

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "Furthermore, the invoice states the manufacturing country is the US, contradicting the Irish origin associated with the SUP-02 register entry."
"US-origin goods cannot claim preferential origin."
"Rejected Hypotheses" lists alternatives, but the analysis does not test whether processing or transformation in Ireland could confer preferential origin independently of the manufacturing country.

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "The preferential-origin claim is NOT supported. The preference claim must be removed and the declaration amended."
"High" confidence is assigned to the conclusion despite the submission identifying missing Procurement evidence and not establishing the applicable origin rule or the full production history.

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "A valid supplier declaration from Procurement" is identified as missing, but the submission does not explain the supplier-declaration lifecycle, whether the expired register reference was replaced, or how manufacturing, processing, origin, and declaration data flow into the broker filing.

"The broker declared the country of origin as United States and claimed preferential tariff treatment." The submission does not investigate whether this is a data-entry inconsistency or a distinction between manufacturing country and preferential origin.

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Instruct the broker to amend the customs declaration ... to remove the preference claim" is a concrete action and the proposed duty-rate check is useful.
"A valid supplier declaration ... [is] missing," so requiring amendment before obtaining or validating the supplier evidence is premature.
"Check if the standard third-country duty rate for CN 90211090 is already 0%" appropriately recognizes that the financial impact is not yet established.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The preference claim must be removed and the declaration amended" is stated as mandatory even though the submission identifies missing supplier and production evidence.

"The invoice states the manufacturing country is the US, contradicting the Irish origin" improperly treats manufacturing country as dispositive of preferential origin; manufacturing location and preferential origin are not necessarily the same.

"US-origin goods cannot claim preferential origin" is overbroad as a general statement and does not establish whether the relevant goods could acquire EU preferential origin through qualifying processing or transformation.
The expired SUP-02 register entry does not, by itself, prove that no replacement, shipment-specific, or other valid supplier evidence exists.

"A valid supplier declaration ... showing that the goods underwent sufficient transformation in the EU" assumes the relevant qualifying route without citing the applicable origin rules or establishing where the transformation occurred.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The records may show a data inconsistency—manufacturing country and broker-declared origin are both listed as US while an Irish preferential-origin basis may exist through qualifying EU processing or a replacement supplier declaration. The evidence supports withholding or verifying the preference claim pending supplier and production records, but not conclusively declaring that the claim is invalid or that amendment is mandatory.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain and verify the shipment-period supplier declaration, production and processing records, and the applicable preferential-origin rule before deciding whether the US manufacturing fact affects EU preferential origin; distinguish manufacturing country, non-preferential origin, and preferential origin explicitly.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "70.6% of release timestamps (185 out of 262) are padded to exactly 02:10:00" — cites batch_release.csv with useful quantitative specificity.
"Northport, Harbor, and Meridian are missing all batch receipt data after 20 July 2026" — cites the relevant file, but does not identify fields, rows, or reconcile source freshness.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "introducing artificial delays" — correctly identifies a timestamp-pattern explanation, but infers the mechanism without requesting event/decision timestamps or an event log.

"The 42 batches on HOLD at Riverbend are a result of a broken QCore data sync" — asserts causality from missing data without testing whether the records were operationally stuck or merely incompletely extracted.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The table labels all major claims "High" confidence and the judgment describes "severe data synchronization failures," despite unresolved timestamp semantics and non-coherent extract timing.
"The SOP target is 24 hours from Lab Complete to Release" — presents a potentially incorrect interpretation of the SOP as certain rather than checking the required-evidence-available definition.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Do NOT build the dashboard using this extract" — prudently prevents use of a potentially misleading KPI.

"A fresh database extract where the sync pipelines ... are fully functional" — useful direction, but it is broad and does not define a reversible validation step, success criteria, or protect against rebuilding the dashboard on still-misdefined timestamps.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "The plant quality teams are experiencing a massive backlog: Rejected" — rejects the strongest operational alternative largely from the same incomplete extracts, without independently testing workflow evidence or stating what evidence could revive it.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "A fresh database extract ... and ... actual granular release times" — requests relevant evidence, but does not prioritize the highest-value query: the timestamp definition and event/decision log, nor explain how that evidence would distinguish workflow delay from interface timing.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The SOP target is stated as Lab Complete to Release; the relevant SOP definition is required evidence available, so the reported 19.1-hour compliance result may be based on the wrong start event.
The 02:10 concentration supports an interface-timestamp anomaly, but "padded ... due to a daily batch update" is a causal inference not established by the extract alone.
The assertion that Riverbend's 42 HOLD batches are caused by a broken QCore sync, and not operational backlog, is overconfident without event-level or independent operational evidence.
The conclusion that all apparent queue volumes are "heavily distorted" is not bounded by source-freshness checks or a coherent point-in-time reconciliation.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The extracts may contain both real workflow delay and interface-commit timing artifacts. The 02:10 concentration can make release-cycle metrics appear worse, while stale or non-coincident snapshots can also create apparent missing receipts and HOLD records; operational backlog therefore remains unresolved rather than rejected.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Request and inspect the timestamp definition plus a small event log linking required-evidence-available, decision/release, and interface-commit times, with extract timestamps. Use it to recalculate a bounded sample KPI before deciding whether the dashboard is unusable or merely requires corrected metric definitions.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The global spare parts catalog data is based on a snapshot from 26 June 2026"; cites source_freshness.csv and maintenance_email(1).txt.
"HA-0026 ... has only 3 units in stock"; cites spare_parts.csv and part_restrictions.csv.
"Revisions B ... must be checked"; cites part_requests.csv and spares_transfer_policy.md.

The submission generally names relevant files, but does not provide row-level quantities, restriction fields, or a complete trace from each request to each classification; it also conflicts with itself by saying HA-0026 has only three units while listing five HA-0026 requests as actionable now.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "All matching part numbers represent actionable transfers: Rejected" because RI-0001 is reserved and HA-0022 has negative stock.
"2 requests must be sourced from NO-0025 or ME-0027, requiring an engineering check."

The submission recognizes that catalog similarity is not sufficient and applies reservation, stock, and revision considerations, but it does not systematically test UOM, qualification, reservation, or criticality constraints for every candidate. The HA-0026 quantity contradiction and the unsupported classification of several semantic candidates weaken the causal chain.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "may lag current local reservations" and "High" confidence for the stale snapshot claim.
"Actionable Now" is assigned to 14 requests despite the stated June 26 snapshot being over a month old and despite the acknowledged three-unit HA-0026 stock limit.

The analyst identifies freshness as decision-relevant and flags engineering checks for revisions, but confidence is not calibrated per transfer and the actionable-now category is too certain given temporal inconsistency and unresolved inventory/reservation status.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "A live stock query in the local CMMS systems" is proposed to verify that the 14 actionable parts remain available.

The recommendation is directionally useful and avoids immediate blind transfer, but it does not propose a reversible semantic-search pilot, define success criteria, require engineering/availability confirmation before movement, or separate candidate value from actionable value. The headline actionable percentage could lead to premature operational decisions.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "All matching part numbers represent actionable transfers: Rejected."
"catalog hits like RI-0001 ... are ... marked as reserved_for_critical_asset" and "HA-0022 has negative stock (-1) due to local lag."

One plausible hypothesis is explicitly rejected using restriction and inventory examples, but the strongest competing explanation—stale or non-coherent extracts causing apparent availability—is only noted, not tested across the classifications. The submission also says PR-260700 has no match while later calling RI-0001 a catalog hit for that request.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "A live stock query in the local CMMS systems" is requested to verify physical stock, reservations, and usage since June 26.

This is relevant and reasonably targeted, but it is not prioritized by highest decision impact and omits the specific engineering, revision, UOM, qualification, and reservation fields needed to discriminate candidate equivalence from transferability.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Out of the 24 ... only $43,120.62 ... is Actionable Now" is overstated because the submission itself states HA-0026 has only three units for five requests, yet marks all five HA-0026 requests actionable now.

"2 requests must be sourced from NO-0025 or ME-0027, requiring an engineering check" is not reflected in the candidate table, which marks PR-260701, PR-260706, PR-260708, PR-260714, and PR-260719 as actionable now.
The submission says "PR-260700 | None" while its rejected-hypothesis section says RI-0001 is a catalog match for PR-260700; this unresolved contradiction undermines the candidate list.
The 14 actionable classifications appear to treat semantic matches and current stock as transfer-ready without demonstrating all revision, UOM, qualification, reservation, and criticality checks.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The semantic search may have generated useful candidate matches, but the evidence supports treating them as candidate value rather than actionable transfers. Given the three-unit HA-0026 constraint, revision mismatches, reservations, negative stock, and a stale/non-coherent enterprise snapshot, the actionable-now share is likely lower and requires live availability plus engineering confirmation.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Rebuild the decision table from request to candidate using current site-level stock, reservation/criticality status, revision, UOM, and qualification fields, explicitly separating candidate matches, engineering-approved equivalents, and physically transferable quantities; then recalculate actionable value with a live snapshot timestamp.
